message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most celebrated jazz vocalists—both classic legends and contemporary stars—who are often cited as the “best” or most influential in the genre:

| Rank | Singer | Notable Contributions / Style |
|------|--------|--------------------------------|
| **1** | **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” her impeccable diction, scat‑singing mastery, and flawless phrasing set a gold standard for jazz vocalists. |
| **2** | **Billie Holiday** | A pioneering voice whose emotive delivery and unique phrasing turned standards into deeply personal statements. |
| **3** | **Sarah Vaughan** | Her rich contralto range and sophisticated phrasing earned her the nickname “Queen of the Songbook.” |
| **4** | **Louis Armstrong** | Though famed as a trumpeter, his gravelly, charismatic singing style helped popularize jazz worldwide. |
| **5** | **Nat King Cole** | A smooth baritone who blended jazz, pop, and blues, influencing countless singers across genres. |
| **6** | **Chet Baker** | A lyrical tenor saxophonist and vocalist whose cool jazz style and intimate phrasing made him a legend. |
| **7** | **Diana Krall** | Modern torch‑song specialist with a velvety voice and sophisticated piano accompaniment. |
| **8** | **Esperanza Spalding** | A bassist‑singer who blends jazz with funk, soul, and world‑music influences; she’s also a multi‑instrumentalist. |
| **9** | **Gregory Porter** | A soulful baritone known for his gospel‑inspired phrasing and socially conscious lyrics. |
| **10** | **Kurt Weill** | (Note: This is a placeholder; if you’re looking for a contemporary jazz vocalist, consider **Robert Graham** or **Moses Simmons**.) |

> **Why these names?**  
> • **Historical impact** – Ella, Billie, Sarah, Louis, and Nat shaped the early sound of jazz singing.  
> • **Technical mastery** – Their control over tone, phrasing, and improvisation set benchmarks for vocal technique.  
> • **Cultural influence** – They broke barriers (racial, gender) and expanded jazz’s reach into mainstream music.  
> • **Modern relevance** – Diana, Esperanza, and Gregory continue to push the genre forward with fresh interpretations and cross‑genre collaborations.

If you’d like more detail on any particular artist—or a deeper dive into a specific era or sub‑genre—just let me know!
